title: Fever Basics for Parents
hook: A fever is a sign the body is fighting infection, not a disease itself — how your child looks and acts often matters more than the exact number on the thermometer.
key_points: Fever is usually defined as a temperature of about 38°C (100.4°F) or higher.
A child's overall behavior — alert and drinking vs. very lethargic — is a key signal alongside the number.
Any fever in a baby under 3 months is treated as urgent: contact a doctor promptly.
Watch for warning signs like trouble breathing, a stiff neck, a non-fading rash, or a hard-to-wake child, and seek care.
content_html: It helps to reframe what a fever is: not an illness, but a sign that the body is doing its job and fighting an infection. A temperature of around 38°C (100.4°F) or higher is generally considered a fever. The exact number matters less than the bigger picture — a child who is alert, drinking, and playing is reassuring even with a fever, while one who is very lethargic warrants more concern.
extra_html: There are clear lines where you don't wait and watch. Any fever in a baby under three months old is treated as urgent — contact a doctor promptly, because young infants can deteriorate quickly. At any age, warning signs like difficulty breathing, a stiff neck, a rash that doesn't fade when pressed, or a child who is very hard to wake mean you should seek medical care right away. This is general guidance from sources like the NHS, not a substitute for advice from your own clinician.

related.title: How Childhood Vaccines Work
related.hook: Vaccines train a child's immune system to recognize a disease in advance, so it can fight off the real thing — and they're scheduled to protect kids when they're most vulnerable.

related.title: Crying Is a Newborn's Main Language
related.hook: Crying is how a newborn communicates every need — and a lot of crying in the first months is normal, peaking around six weeks and easing after that.

flashcards.prompt: A fever in a baby younger than 3 months should be treated as:

choices.text: Normal and best left to pass on its own

flashcards.explanation_html: Young infants can become unwell quickly, so any fever under 3 months of age warrants prompt medical advice.

flashcards.prompt: What is a fever, and what does it tell you?
flashcards.back_html: A raised body temperature (about 38°C / 100.4°F or higher) — a sign the body is fighting an infection, not a disease in itself.

flashcards.prompt: Alongside the thermometer reading, what's an important thing to watch?

choices.text: How the child looks and behaves — alert and drinking vs. very lethargic
Only the exact decimal of the temperature
Whether the room feels warm to you

flashcards.explanation_html: A child's overall behavior is a key signal. Warning signs like trouble breathing or a non-fading rash mean seek care regardless of the number.
